title: NFR-004 timeout discipline: a hung upstream is abandoned at the deadline and recorded honestly
risk: A hung connector call blocks a worker forever, so queues back up and the customer waits indefinitely with no honest status anywhere.
preconditions: Namespace gov-nfr-<case_id>-<worker_id>; NFR verification runs against the offline gateway with mock SoR and channel boundaries.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; failure, outage and crash injections are scripted at the substituted boundary, never faked inside the assertion.
The mock ERP is scripted to accept the connection and never respond.

steps.action: Issue the lookup against the hanging upstream
steps.expected: The call is abandoned at the configured deadline (2001 ms on the injected clock) rather than waiting indefinitely.
The record shows a timeout error preserving the upstream identity and the elapsed time; it is not marked success.

steps.action: Check the worker and queue state
steps.expected: The worker is released and the task moves to a retry or failure state; no worker remains blocked on the call.
The retry returns ORD-A-1 details and the final record reconciles to one honest successful attempt.

assertions: The deadline is enforced deterministically using the injected clock: the call does not hang past it.
Timed-out attempts are recorded as failures with elapsed time, never as successes.
The worker is not leaked: the pool returns to its pre-call capacity.
After recovery, exactly one successful attempt and one failure attempt are recorded for the task.
forbidden: No timeout at all so the worker hangs.
Reporting a timeout as a success because the connection was accepted.
Leaking the worker slot on timeout.
evidence: Timeout error record with elapsed time and upstream identity.
Worker capacity before and after the call.
Recovery attempt record and the final order payload.
cleanup: Restore the mock ERP script and delete gov- task rows.
automation: Core PEP, rules engine, audit writer, idempotency store and worker lease logic run as real code under test; only ERP/WMS, channel gateways, Redis and the model provider are substituted. Faults are injected at those boundaries and waits are condition-based on persisted state. Deadline enforcement uses the injected clock so the case cannot pass by finishing early in real time.
